title: Hindley-Milner inference
hook: How does Hindley-Milner infer types with unification and no annotations?

scenes.caption: Every unknown gets a fresh type variable, and each operator contributes constraints.
scenes.narration: To infer fun x arrow x plus one, give x a fresh type variable alpha. Plus has type int to int to int, which constrains alpha.

elements.text:
fun x -> x + 1

x   : alpha
(+) : int -> int -> int
alpha ~ int

scenes.caption: Unification solves constraints: variables bind to types, and constructors must match structurally.
scenes.narration: Unification solves the equations. A variable binds to a type, matching constructors unify argument by argument, and int against bool is a type error.

elements.text:
unify(a, t):    bind a := t
unify(T a.., T b..):
  unify each pair
unify(int, bool):
  type error

scenes.caption: The occurs check rejects infinite types such as alpha = alpha -> beta.
scenes.narration: Before binding a variable, the occurs check ensures it is absent from the other type. That rejects x applied to x, which needs alpha equal to alpha arrow beta.

elements.text:
fun x -> x x

x : alpha
alpha ~ alpha -> beta
alpha occurs in alpha -> beta: reject.

scenes.caption: Let-bound names are generalized to polymorphic schemes and instantiated freshly at each use.
scenes.narration: At a let, free type variables are generalized, so id is polymorphic. Each use instantiates fresh variables, so id one and id true both typecheck.

elements.text:
let id = fun x -> x in
(id 1, id true)   (* ok *)

fun f -> (f 1, f true)
(* error: f is monomorphic *)

scenes.caption: Algorithm W infers principal types; implementations use union-find and levels for speed.
scenes.narration: Algorithm W yields the principal, most general type. Implementations use union-find for variables and levels for cheap generalization. This core underlies ML and OCaml.

items: Worst case is exponential, rare in practice

takeaway: Hindley-Milner assigns type variables, solves equality constraints by unification with an occurs check, and generalizes at let to infer principal types without annotations.
